Thanks Daniel — great questions. High level answers and proposed next steps below. TL;DR: we recommend a focused parity run using your sample tagset + our standardized prompt bundle; acceptance = no statistically significant drop in human eval win-rate beyond 5% vs baseline (we can make this stricter if you prefer).

1) What parity means (proposal)
- Functional parity: for the fraud prompts you shared, the open model should match the baseline on precision/recall within an acceptable band (+/- 5% by default) and show no new high-severity false positives in adjudicated samples.
- Human evaluation: a blind review with your SME adjudicators where open model outputs are preferred at least as often as baseline within the margin.
- Latency/cost SLOs: median token latency below 250ms for inference at your 95th percentile QPS (we'll size accordingly).

2) How we run the evaluation
- Option A (recommended): You provide a redacted 10k-sample subset (S3 link or secure Share). We run the full benchmark in our dedicated sandbox; logs and model artifacts are scoped to the job and retention is configurable (default 30 days).
- Option B: we ship a test harness and your team runs it on-prem (we can provide Docker + instructions).

3) Prompt set + artifacts (attached)
- Attached: blueharbor_prompt_set_v1.json (your sample prompts + templated variants), open-vs-prop-benchmarks-20260822.csv (example output format), redwood-proposed-mop.pdf (method of procedure and eval gates).

4) Suggested acceptance thresholds (initial)
- Precision within -5% of baseline, recall within -7% (due to tooling bias); human eval win-rate delta <= 5% against baseline; no high-severity FP introduced in >0.2% of cases.

5) Timeline & next steps
- If we get the sample by Tue EOD (Aug 24) we can run a 72-hour pass, share preliminary results by Aug 27, and schedule a 30-min review call the same day.
- NDA: if you want us to run on raw data, please sign the attached NDA link (DocuSign) or request a hosted-sandbox flow.

I'll loop Rishi to scope the benchmark run and Neha to cover commercial questions.

Best,
Naomi

Adding tech detail and practical runbook:

- Benchmark harness: we'll use our internal harness with deterministic seed control and the prompt bundle Naomi attached. Metrics collected: P/R, AUC, top-N token overlap, and a small blind human-eval slice (n=500).
- Model candidates we recommend to trial (short list):
  * open-1.3B-rlf (fast, lower-cost)
  * open-7B-q4f16 (expected best quality/cost balance)
  * open-13B-qat (closest to your baseline on small evals we've run)
  * fallback: proprietary-small (licensed baseline) for hybrid routing during canary runs.
- Resource plan: 2 full parallel workers (13B quantized) for the 72-hour run; estimated compute cost = ~$6.5k (we'll firm this after we inspect your distribution).
- Data handling: sandboxed job — raw inputs kept in encrypted ephemeral storage, results exported with redacted identifiers unless you request full artifact retention. Retention default 30 days; we can extend to 90 on request.
- Acceptance gating: automated statistical test (bootstrap) with configurable alpha. We propose alpha=0.05.

Request for you: provide the redacted sample (S3 link or secure Share) plus a quick note on the distribution skew (fraud types, class imbalance) so we can pick prompts for targeted slices.

I'll stand up the run the moment we have the sample and NDA status.

—Rishi
